_comment: Functions the original build did NOT compile with the default toolchain.
tools/agbcc/bin/ holds two compilers. The Makefile defined CC1_OLD for
old_agbcc from the start and never referenced it; wave 10 found out why it
is there. The sound and flash libraries came out of the SDK prebuilt with
their own settings and were dropped into the game's build, which is the
same layout every other GBA tree has.
This file is the single source of truth for that. tools/agbenv.py applies
it so trymatch.py and compile_probe judge a candidate the way the ROM was
actually built, and tools/gen_overrides_mk.py turns it into target-specific
make variables. Both must agree: an override known only to the build makes
every later wave re-attempt an already-solved function and conclude it
cannot be matched.
An entry needs the same standard of evidence as data/asm-resident.json --
a byte-for-byte match under the named configuration, and a note on what the
default configuration does differently. 'It matched when I changed a flag'
with no mechanism is how a real bug gets papered over.
Blast radius, measured by recompiling all 520 promoted files both ways:
old_agbcc changes 100 of them, dropping -fforce-addr changes 17. Neither
is a candidate for a global change. Per-file it costs nothing -- no
promoted file between 0x0806F710 and 0x080745C0 differs under old_agbcc,
and none above 0x08063A3C differs without -fforce-addr.
CONSTRAINT: an overridden function must sit in a .c file of its own. The
build applies flags per object, so a shared file would silently recompile
its neighbours with the wrong toolchain. tools/gen_overrides_mk.py fails
loudly rather than emitting a rule that would do that.

sub_080713F8.reason: m4a MPlayTempoControl. old_agbcc keeps a member re-read live instead of coalescing it with the value just stored there, and substitutes the stored register rather than emitting a reload: `mplayInfo->tempoU = tempo; ... mplayInfo->tempoD * mplayInfo->tempoU` emits a second ldrh under agbcc and reuses the register under old_agbcc. That extra live value is what forces the `adds r0, r1, #0` copy, the r4 allocation and the `push {r4, lr}` frame -- all three of which the default build was missing at once. Parked at 32 of 40 bytes for two waves against the source axis, which was never the axis. old_agbcc rejects -fprologue-bugfix outright.

sub_08071564.reason: m4a MP_clear_modM, the compiled twin of the hand-written sub_08070300. Under agbcc a two-armed if/else assigning one object collapses to 'store the else value, conditionally overwrite' -- one arm, no unconditional b, one instruction shorter. old_agbcc does not do that rewrite: both arms and the b survive, the shared operand is loaded after the merge, and the branchless arm's constant stays as a second, dead movs. That one rewrite was the entire 4-byte deficit, after eighteen source spellings had been probed against it.

sub_0808AD6C.reason: SetReadFlash1 -- the flash library, not the game. Relocates a 4-byte THUMB routine into RAM and publishes it through gUnknown_03000F6C with the THUMB bit set. -fforce-addr is what made agbcc keep the sub_0808AD68 pool word in a register across the eors that clobbers it; without the flag it rematerialises, which is the double load the ROM has. Either compiler works. Parked at 85.7% across two waves and a permuter run, all of it spent on the source.
